questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law / attended the meeting / as his health is not more good.

options.text: Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law
as his health is not more good

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 4 i.e. this part of the sentence contains a grammatical error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "his health is not more good" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be "their health is not good anymore" or "their health is no longer good".

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law attended the meeting as their health is not good anymore.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "More good" is incorrect; "better" should be used for comparisons, or expressions like "not good anymore" should be used to indicate a negative change in state.
 
• When talking about health deterioration, "not good anymore" indicates the current state effectively.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to

form a meaningful sentence.

(P) kindness and empathy

(Q) in a world that can be

(O) bring light and positivity

(R) harsh and challenging
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (3)** i.e. **QRPO**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Q** in a world that can be" begins the sentence by setting up the context.
 
• **R** harsh and challenging" continues the context by describing the nature of the world.
 
• **P** kindness and empathy" introduces the key elements that are needed in such a world.
 
• **O** bring light and positivity" concludes the sentence by describing the effect of kindness and empathy.

Therefore, the correct answer is **QRPO.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (PORQ):** This option places kindness and empathy first, which doesn't provide the necessary context before introducing the main subject.
 
• **Option 2 (ROQP):** This option disrupts the logical flow by starting with the description of the world before introducing kindness and empathy.
 
• **Option 4 (QROP):** This option is close but ends with the incomplete phrase "bring light and positivity" instead of the intended effect.

questions.question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. 'recieved'.

• The word **"recieved"** is incorrectly spelt; the correct spelling is "received". (प्राप्त किया)

 
 
• **Example: **She received an award for her outstanding performance.

• **Example: **He received a letter from his old friend yesterday.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. 'recieved'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example: **His performance in the play was outstanding.

• **Example:** She did an outstanding job on the project.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To read between the lines

options.text: To understand more than what the words suggest

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To read between the lines"** means to understand more than what the words suggest; it involves perceiving the hidden or underlying meaning behind the words. (शब्दों से अधिक समझना)

 
 
• **Example: **When she said she was fine, he read between the lines and knew she was actually upset.
 
 
 
• **"To underline some words"** refers to physically drawing a line under words for emphasis. (कुछ शब्दों को रेखांकित करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The teacher asked us to underline the important points in the text.
 
 
 
• **"To read differently"** refers to interpreting or understanding text in a different manner. (अलग तरीके से पढ़ना)
 
 
• **Example: **She read the poem differently, finding new meanings in the verses.
 
 
 
• **"To read aloud to public"** means to read something out loud for an audience to hear. (जनता के सामने जोर से पढ़ना)
 
 
• **Example: **The author read aloud her new book to the audience at the event.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To underline some words** (कुछ शब्दों को रेखांकित करना): Drawing a line under words for emphasis.

 
 
• **Example:** The teacher asked us to underline the important points in the text.
 
 
 
• **To read differently** (अलग तरीके से पढ़ना): Interpreting or understanding text in a different manner.
 
 
• **Example: **She read the poem differently, finding new meanings in the verses.
 
 
 
• **To read aloud to public** (जनता के सामने जोर से पढ़ना): Reading something out loud for an audience to hear.
 
 
• **Example:** The author read aloud her new book to the audience at the event.

questions.question:
Select the option that can replace the underlined phrase and make the sentence grammatically correct.

The programme on TV __was now shown the blurring faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre.__

options.text: were now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre.
was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre
were now showing the blurring faces of the inmates from the rehabilitation centre
was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates upon the rehabilitation centre

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 i.e.this part of the sentence needs to be substituted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct phrase should be "was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre".
 
• The verb "was" must be used instead of "were" to match the singular noun "programme".
 
• The past participle "blurred" correctly describes the state of the faces being shown.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *The programme on TV **was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The verb and subject must agree in number: "programme" is singular, so it requires "was".
 
• "Blurred" is the correct form to describe the state resulting from the action of blurring.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.

A. It contains high levels of Vitamin A and D.

B. Cod liver oil is thus used to treat arthritis.

C. It is extracted from the liver of cod fish.

D. Cod liver oil is a nutritional supplement.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (3)** i.e. **DCAB**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **D** Cod liver oil is a nutritional supplement" introduces the main subject, cod liver oil.
 
• **C** It is extracted from the liver of cod fish" provides information on the source of cod liver oil.
 
• **A** It contains high levels of Vitamin A and D" details the nutritional contents of the oil.
 
• **B** Cod liver oil is thus used to treat arthritis" concludes by explaining a practical application of the supplement.

Therefore, the correct answer is **DCAB.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (ABCD):** This option starts with the nutritional content without introducing the main subject first.
 
• **Option 2 (CBAD):** This option describes the source first, followed by nutritional content and use, but it doesn't introduce the main subject at the beginning.
 
• **Option 4 (BACD):** This option discusses the application first, before defining and describing the main subject properly.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Each candidate was making tall promises.

options.text: Tall promises were being made by each candidate.
Tall promises are made by each candidate.
Tall promises will be made by each candidate.
Tall promises are being made by each candidate.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: Subject + was/were + present participle (verb+ing) + object.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Each candidate was making tall promises."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "tall promises" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "was making" to "were being made" (past continuous passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "each candidate".

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Tall promises were being made by each candidate."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"Tall promises are made by each candidate." – Incorrect tense (present simple passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"Tall promises will be made by each candidate." – Incorrect tense (future simple passive).
 
• **Option 4: **"Tall promises are being made by each candidate." – Incorrect tense (present continuous passive).

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Rahul thinks he is as smarter as his friends in the class.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 i.e.this part of the sentence contains an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "he is as smarter as" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• The correct comparative structure is "as + adjective + as" when comparing two things that are equal in some way.
 
• Therefore, it should be "he is as smart as" instead of "he is as smarter as".

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *Rahul thinks he is as smart as his friends in the class.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The structure "as + adjective + as" is used to make comparisons indicating equality.
 
• "Smarter" indicates a comparative degree and does not fit in the "as ... as" structure where the positive degree adjective "smart" should be used.

questions.question:
In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent statement.

O: population is expected to triple in

P: the next 50 years

Q: among the world's poorest countries

R: population shrinkage in that period

S: whereas many rich countries will see
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (4)** i.e. **QOPSR**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Q** among the world's poorest countries" sets the context for the population trend being discussed.
 
• **O** population is expected to triple in" describes the expected population growth in these countries.
 
• **P** the next 50 years" specifies the time frame for the population increase.
 
• **S** whereas many rich countries will see" introduces the contrast to the first statement.
 
• **R** population shrinkage in that period" concludes by describing the opposite trend in rich countries.

Therefore, the correct answer is **QOPSR.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (POSQR):** This option does not accurately set up the contrast between the two trends.
 
• **Option 2 (RSOPQ):** This option starts with the contrasting trend without introducing the primary context first.
 
• **Option 3 (SPORQ):** This option begins with the contrasting trend but does not logically follow with the expected population growth sequence.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.

The car was repaired by the mechanic.

options.text: The mechanic has repaired the car.
The mechanic is repairing the car.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The subject of the active voice sentence becomes the object of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The car was repaired by the mechanic."
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the original subject "the mechanic" at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• Change the passive verb form "was repaired" to "repaired" (simple past active).
 
• Keep the object "the car" after the verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The mechanic repaired the car."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The mechanic repairs the car." – Incorrect tense (present simple active).
 
• **Option 2: **"The mechanic has repaired the car." – Incorrect tense (present perfect active).
 
• **Option 3: **"The mechanic is repairing the car." – Incorrect tense (present continuous active).
